# Partner Fit and Referral Brief

**Partner organization or operator:** [Name]  
**Relationship owner:** [Name]  
**Date reviewed:** [Date]

## 1. Fit Hypothesis

Describe the buyer or client situation in which a partnership would create a clearer, safer, or more complete client path. Do not treat audience overlap alone as partnership fit.

| Question | Response |
| --- | --- |
| What client need can this relationship serve better? | |
| Which party owns which part of the client outcome? | |
| What is explicitly outside the relationship? | |
| What client risk could this partnership introduce? | |
| What evidence supports the fit? | |

## 3. Referral Quality Standard

A referral should include a named buyer or operator, a real stated need, permission to introduce, and enough context to avoid a generic sales pitch. Referrals are not purchased, fabricated, or represented as customer endorsement.

| Required referral context | Provided? | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Permission to introduce | ☐ | |
| Buyer role and operating context | ☐ | |
| Stated decision or need | ☐ | |
| Timeline/constraint if known | ☐ | |
| Appropriate first step | ☐ | |
| Relationship owner | ☐ | |

## 4. Review and Exit

| Review question | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Did the relationship create clearer client value? | |
| Were responsibilities and handoffs reliable? | |
| Did it create unacceptable client, data, brand, or team risk? | |
| Continue, change, pause, or end? | |
